question: Adaptive servo-ventilation (ASV) is a safe and effective treatment for central sleep apnoea in patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤45%) and is recommended as first-line therapy in this population.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. ASV is CONTRAINDICATED in HFrEF with LVEF ≤45% and central sleep apnoea due to increased mortality demonstrated in the SERVE-HF trial. This is a classic high-stakes exam trap: ASV appears logical (breathing support) but causes harm in this specific phenotype.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is false. The SERVE-HF trial demonstrated that ASV significantly increases cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in HFrEF patients (LVEF ≤45%) with predominant central sleep apnoea. ASV is therefore contraindicated in this population. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for obstructive sleep apnoea does not carry this risk.
